input.rationale: Refinement of the wedge investigation after its repair boundary was executed. The recorded availability witness is a three-voter cluster losing its one-failure tolerance; the same mechanism implies a more general statement that one execution can test cheaply by widening the same staging: the wedged replica permanently occupies one slot of the commitment quorum at its stuck index, so it costs exactly one unit of failure margin regardless of configuration size. In a five-voter cluster the source arithmetic says the wedged replica is harmless while the other four answer (the quorum match index is still the healthy value) and becomes fatal only when enough other voters are gone that the wedged index enters the quorum. Recording the refinement now, with the harness change deferred to the next turn, keeps the question inside the same investigation rather than opening a variant as an independent defect.

investigations.hypothesis: Two-part account, now with its margin generalisation. First, as recorded: the conflict path deletes the conflicting suffix and then stores the replacements; if StoreLogs returns an allowed error the handler returns before setLastLog, so the cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix. Second, as witnessed: because the entry loop trusts that cached index, the replacement entries are never stored again, the leader's retries cannot repair it, and the replica stays wedged until a restart or a snapshot. Third, the margin generalisation to be measured: a wedged replica holds one commitment slot at its stuck index for as long as it remains a voter, so the cluster loses exactly one unit of failure margin - in a three-voter configuration a single further voter loss makes new entries uncommittable, and in a five-voter configuration the same should hold only after two further voter losses, with commit still progressing while four voters answer.
investigations.discriminator: Extend the same staging to five voters with the fault wrapper on the initial leader: run the legal partition, divergence and higher-term replacement history with the injected StoreLogs error, confirm the wedge, then remove healthy voters one at a time and apply a client entry after each removal, recording the leader's commit index, the apply future and every node's state at each step. The control is the same five-voter staging without the store error. The expected discriminator is the step at which commit stops: in the faulted case it should stop exactly one voter later than in the control, and the wedged node's store and certificate should be unchanged across the steps.
limitations: The margin generalisation is a source-derived prediction until the five-voter execution is interpreted; the three-voter observation remains the witnessed part.
Only configurations whose quorum includes the wedged replica can be affected; the measurement covers three and five voters, not every size.

knowledge.statement: commitment keeps one match index per voter of the current configuration and takes the quorum match index as the middle of the sorted values, so a voter whose stored log can never advance holds its slot at the stuck index for as long as the configuration stands. The wedged replica therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin: the remaining voters must be able to form a quorum on their own, which in a three-voter configuration is impossible once one other voter is gone and in a five-voter configuration only becomes impossible when two other voters are gone.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; a voter whose durable log is stuck below the leader's committed prefix while it remains a member of configurations.latest; commitment.setConfiguration has been applied for that configuration.

investigations.question: Does the leader's explicit leadership-transfer path verify that the caller-supplied target can acquire leadership (i.e. is a Voter in the latest configuration), and if it does not, what happens to the incumbent leader, to the target, and to the returned future when the target is a legal non-voter member added with AddNonvoter?
investigations.hypothesis: The transfer path validates only that the target is not the leader itself (raft.go 2191-2196) and that a replication state exists for it (777-783). Replication state exists for every server in configurations.latest, including Nonvoters (the startStopReplication loop at 587 has no suffrage filter), so a non-voter target is accepted end to end. The leader then replicates up to its own last index and sends TimeoutNow; timeoutNow (2208-2215) has no term, no state and no suffrage test, so the target campaigns at term+1 with the transfer flag. Every voter adopts the higher term and steps down before rejecting the vote because the candidate is not a voter (1670-1683), and the candidate can never win because electSelf only asks and self-votes Voters (2015). Predicted observations: the transfer future still reports success, the target never becomes Leader, and the incumbent loses leadership and is replaced by whichever voter campaigns next. The positive control (identical call to a voter) should transfer leadership to the named target.
investigations.discriminator: One execution, two cases. Case A (control): 3-voter cluster, LeadershipTransferToServer to a voter; the target should become Leader. Case B: same cluster plus a node added with AddNonvoter and verified caught up; LeadershipTransferToServer to that non-voter. The future value alone does not discriminate, since both cases may return success: the decisive difference is whether the named target ever reaches Leader and whether the incumbent's leadership survives. Vote evidence comes from the library's own observer stream (RequestVoteRequest records candidate ID, term, log position and transfer flag) plus timestamped state/term sampling, so the effect can be attributed to suffrage rather than to generic transfer flakiness.
limitations: Source reading establishes the guards and their absence; the concrete sequence, the future value and the recovery time are predictions until the retained execution is interpreted.

Contention: requestVote's deliberate high-term step-down for a non-voter candidate (comment citing hashicorp/raft#526) shows the library anticipates a campaigning non-voter; it does not show that the library's own transfer API may create that state from a legal caller input.

investigations.question: When a follower receives entries that conflict with a suffix it already holds and the LogStore returns an allowed error for the replacement write, what does the node's in-memory last-log certificate (lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm) describe afterwards, is that certificate used by the node's own vote producers and vote decisions, and does anything repair it before the node next campaigns?
investigations.hypothesis: Two-part account. First, as recorded: the conflict path deletes the conflicting suffix from disk and then stores the replacements; if StoreLogs returns an allowed error the handler returns before setLastLog, so the cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix and the node's public LastIndex, its vote credentials and its prev-log judgments all reflect it. Second, and stronger: the certificate is not merely misreported, it blocks recovery. The entry loop uses the cached lastLogIdx (from getLastLog) to decide whether an incoming entry is already stored: for any entry with entry.Index <= cached lastLogIdx it calls logs.GetLog on that index instead of treating it as new. After the truncation those indices are gone from the store, so GetLog fails, the handler logs 'failed to get log entry' and returns - the replacement entries are never written, and no branch updates the certificate. The leader's reject branch floors nextIndex at 1 (max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1)), so it keeps re-sending a request that the follower keeps rejecting for the same reason: the same reject path is re-entered, the follower stores nothing, and no code path re-reads the log store or repairs the certificate. Predicted observations: the certificate stays above the store's real last index indefinitely; the follower's log store never regains the missing indices; the leader's nextIndex for that peer settles at 1 and stays there; and the only in-library repairs (NewRaft re-reading the store at startup, or an InstallSnapshot) are not triggered by this state.
investigations.discriminator: Stage a legal single-cluster history: 4 voters, the initial leader A is partitioned, A appends entries locally while the majority {B,C,D} elects a new leader at a higher term and commits different entries at the same indices; then arm a legal LogStore wrapper on A (all StoreLogs calls fail with an error, an allowed return from the interface) and heal. Compare, over a bounded window of at least two seconds: A's cached certificate (getLastEntry/LastIndex) against A's store contents (FirstIndex/LastIndex and GetLog of the certificate index); whether A's store ever regains the missing indices or its commit/applied index advances; and the leader's nextIndex for A over time, to show whether the reject/retry cycle restores the same blocking request (nextIndex floored at 1) with no enabled repair. The control is the same conflict and heal with a healthy store: A converges (certificate equals the store's last index and the entries are stored). To distinguish the blocking cause from a mere certificate report, the control must show convergence with the fault absent, and the faulted case must show the store never advancing even though the leader keeps sending.
limitations: The stronger safety consequence remains unclaimed for the reason already recorded: a truncation only happens when the incoming term is not older than the receiver's current term, so the deleted suffix's terms are lower than the truncating leader's, and any voter that accepted that leader's entries has a higher last term and denies the stale claimant.

The wedge claim is a source-derived prediction until executed; the two events it needs (a conflicting suffix truncation and an allowed StoreLogs error in that exact window) must both be staged and stated, and the observation window must be long enough to show the same blocking request being re-entered rather than a one-off rejection.

history.question: When a follower receives entries that conflict with a suffix it already holds and the LogStore returns an allowed error for the replacement write, what does the node's in-memory last-log certificate (lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm) describe afterwards, is that certificate used by the node's own vote producers and vote decisions, and does anything repair it before the node next campaigns?
history.hypothesis: The conflict path first deletes the conflicting suffix from disk (DeleteRange succeeds, which also drops the cache in LogCache), then calls StoreLogs for the replacement entries. When StoreLogs returns an allowed error the handler logs, returns, and never reaches the setLastLog call at the end of the success path; nothing else in the receive path repairs it, and the same senders were never updated, so the in-memory certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix. The node therefore reports a last index and last term that its durable log no longer contains: LastIndex() overstates the store's LastIndex(), the node's own RequestVote advertises that position, and the node's up-to-date judgments use it. Prediction to be measured: the certificate stays inconsistent (no repair) until some later AppendEntries succeeds, and the inconsistency is visible in a real vote request the node emits when it campaigns.
history.discriminator: Build the conflicting-suffix prefix from real producers rather than supplied bytes: two real clusters whose leaders hold different terms, joined at the transport level, so that the higher-term leader legitimately appends entries over an index where the other node holds a lower-term entry; give the receiving node a legal LogStore wrapper that fails exactly one StoreLogs call (an allowed error return, not corruption). Then compare, from the same run: the node's reported LastIndex()/last-entry position against the store's actual LastIndex() and a GetLog of the reported index; the same comparison after later successful AppendEntries, to show whether the inconsistency is transient or persists; and the last_log_index/last_log_term the node puts in the RequestVote it emits when it is next left without a leader, read from the observer stream. A control that lets the same StoreLogs call succeed isolates the store error as the cause of the inconsistency.
limitations: The stronger safety consequence is deliberately not claimed: a truncation only occurs when the incoming term is not older than the receiver's current term (appendEntries returns early for an older term), so the deleted suffix's terms are lower than the truncating leader's and any voter holding that leader's entries has a higher last term and denies the stale claimant.

The trigger needs two events in sequence - an allowed store write error inside an exact window, and no later successful AppendEntries before the node campaigns - so the harness must state and hold both, and the claim is bounded to that history.

investigations.question: In the growth sequence the library documents (bootstrap a single voter, then AddVoter the next server), what happens to commitment, leadership and further elections if the newly named server is not running yet, and does the cluster recover once that server appears at the announced address?
investigations.hypothesis: appendConfigurationEntry installs the next configuration as configurations.latest and calls commitment.setConfiguration before the entry is committed, and the new server's match index starts at 0. In the 1-to-2 growth step the new configuration's quorum is 2, so the configuration entry (and any later entry) can never reach a quorum match index while that server is absent. checkLeaderLease counts the voters of the latest configuration, sees one contacted server against a quorum of two, and steps the leader down after the lease expires; elections then need a quorum of the same latest configuration, which the single surviving server cannot supply, so no leader is elected and the cluster stops accepting new entries. The caller's AddVoter timeout does not cover this: requestConfigChange only uses it to bound the enqueue, and the returned future resolves when the configuration commits. Prediction: the cluster stays without a leader and without progress until the announced server appears, at which point the configuration entry commits and the cluster resumes.
investigations.discriminator: Build a real single-voter cluster with MakeCluster(1), obtain the address of a future server from a fresh in-memory transport that is deliberately not wired to the cluster, and call AddVoter on the leader with that address. Record, over a bounded window: the configuration entry index against the leader's commit index, the leader's state and term, whether it ever leaves leadership, whether another node ever becomes leader, whether a later Apply completes, and the future's resolution. Then wire the announced server in (starting a raft on that address with its own empty store) and record whether the configuration commits and progress resumes. The control is the same growth step with the server started and wired before the call, which isolates the absent server as the cause rather than the growth step itself.
limitations: Adding a voter whose process is not running is the caller's input, so the argument rests on the library's own documentation of this sequence and on its stated staging/promotion behaviour, not on an invented caller mistake.

The arithmetic is configuration dependent: growing 2 to 3 or 3 to 4 keeps a quorum among the survivors, so the claim is scoped to configurations whose new quorum cannot be met without the absent server, of which the documented 1-to-2 start is the example.
The transient unavailability window in the observed run will be bounded by the lease and election timeouts; the source-derived part is that no self-repair exists while the server is absent.

knowledge.statement: For an explicit leadership transfer (LeadershipTransferToServer) the leader accepts the caller-supplied target if and only if a followerReplication entry exists for that ServerID in leaderState.replState; the only rejection is a target equal to the local ID ('cannot transfer leadership to itself'). No suffrage test is applied at the API, at initiateLeadershipTransfer, or at the leaderLoop hand-off to leadershipTransfer.
knowledge.conditions: protocolVersion >= 3, node is in Leader state and processing the leadershipTransferCh case on the main thread; the caller supplies an ID present in configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: startStopReplication starts a followerReplication goroutine for every server in configurations.latest whose ID differs from the local ID, with no suffrage filter, so leaderState.replState (the map consulted by the explicit transfer path and by pickServer) also contains Nonvoter members. pickServer, by contrast, skips 'server.Suffrage != Voter', so the targetless transfer path cannot select a non-voter.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state, after appendConfigurationEntry/setLatestConfiguration followed by startStopReplication.

knowledge.statement: On receiving a TimeoutNowRequest a node clears its known leader, sets its state to Candidate and sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer to true, then acknowledges. The handler performs no term comparison (TimeoutNowRequest carries no term), no state check, no suffrage check on the receiver, and no check that the sender is the current leader or a configuration member; runCandidate then skips pre-vote for such a candidate and calls electSelf directly.
knowledge.conditions: The RPC passes checkRPCHeader (protocol version range) and is dispatched from processRPC on the main thread.

knowledge.statement: In requestVote, when a RequestVote arrives with req.Term > currentTerm the receiver first steps down (setState(Follower)) and adopts the higher term, and only afterwards rejects the request because the candidate is not a Voter ('rejecting vote request since node is not a voter'), returning Granted false. Because the step-down precedes the rejection, a term-advancing vote request from an unelectable candidate still removes the receiver from leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a Voter or Leader with a non-empty configurations.latest.Servers, and the candidate passes the inConfiguration check.

knowledge.statement: In appendEntries, when a received entry conflicts with one the node already stores, the node deletes the range [entry.Index, lastLogIdx] via logs.DeleteRange, then stores the replacement entries via logs.StoreLogs. If StoreLogs returns an error the handler logs 'failed to append to logs' and returns before any setLastLog call: the in-memory lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm keep the values they had before the deletion (the code marks this with a TODO), and no other branch in the receive path restores them. The response for that request is left with Success false.
knowledge.conditions: Follower/Candidate state; a.Term not older than the node's current term; at least one received entry whose index is at or below the node's last log index and whose term differs from the stored entry; and an error return from logs.StoreLogs for that call.

knowledge.statement: The in-memory last-log certificate is read through raftState.getLastEntry (and getLastIndex, which takes the maximum of lastLogIndex and lastSnapshotIndex, so a snapshot does not mask a stale log index). Its consumers are: electSelf and preElectSelf, which put it in RequestVoteRequest/RequestPreVoteRequest as LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm; requestVote/requestPreVote, which use it to decide whether to grant a vote; appendEntries, which compares it against PrevLogEntry to validate a leader's previous entry; and Raft.LastIndex, the public accessor. None of these consult the LogStore.
knowledge.conditions: Any node, whenever it campaigns or answers a vote request or validates an AppendEntries previous entry.

knowledge.statement: In the appendEntries entry loop the comparison 'entry.Index > lastLogIdx' uses lastLogIdx read from the in-memory certificate (getLastLog), not from the log store. For an entry at or below that cached index the handler calls logs.GetLog(entry.Index) and returns immediately if it errors, so once the conflicting suffix has been deleted from the store, any re-sent entry covering those indices makes the handler return before StoreLogs is reached. The certificate is never re-derived from the store inside this handler.
knowledge.conditions: Follower or Candidate state with at least one entry in the request whose index is at or below the cached last log index while that index is absent from the store (the state produced by a failed StoreLogs immediately after a conflicting-suffix deletion).

knowledge.statement: On an unsuccessful AppendEntries response the leader sets the peer's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1). When the follower's response carries a LastLog at or above the leader's index, the value settles at 1 (or at the floor) and the leader re-sends the same request, so a follower that rejects for a self-inflicted reason is re-driven with an identical request rather than a snapshot; ErrLogNotFound leading to SEND_SNAP is only produced from the leader's own log store, not from the follower's response.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the follower responds Success=false with a LastLog hint at or above the leader's last index.

knowledge.statement: A single allowed error return from LogStore.StoreLogs in the call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge: its durable log keeps the truncated state (its last index falls to the last surviving index before the conflict), its cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix, its commit and applied indexes stop advancing, and no further StoreLogs call is even attempted, so removing the error afterwards does not restore progress.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, one follower holding an isolated uncommitted tail appended at an earlier term, a higher-term leader with committed replacement entries at the same indices, and exactly one allowed StoreLogs error on the replacement write; the fault may be removed afterwards without changing the outcome. In the observed run the same history with a healthy store converged inside the window (store 1..5, certificate (5,3), commit and applied 5) while the faulted node stayed at store last 2, certificate (4,2) and commit and applied 2 for 2.7 s.

knowledge.statement: When the wedged replica from the conflict-truncation store-error state is one of three voters, the cluster cannot commit any new entry after a single further voter loss: the leader accepts the entry into its own log (store and certificate advance to the new index) but its commit index stays at the value it had before and the client's apply future never completes, whereas the control run of the identical history without the store error commits the same entry as soon as the peer-loss phase begins. The wedged replica's store last index and StoreLogs attempt counter are unchanged across the phase, so its match index cannot advance and the quorum of match indexes can no longer include the new entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport; one voter left in the conflict-truncation store-error state (store truncated, cached certificate stale, no further store writes); one further voter removed; one client entry applied on the remaining leader. Observed for 1500 ms with 25 ms sampling, with the matching control run in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, without waiting for it to commit, sets configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration, which rebuilds the match-index map so that every voter of the new configuration is counted, with servers that have never answered starting at 0. The quorum decisions for commitment therefore use the new configuration from that moment, while configurations.committed still describes the old one.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; any successful configuration change request (AddVoter, AddNonvoter, DemoteVoter, RemoveServer) whose entry has been appended but not yet committed.

knowledge.statement: Both the leader lease check and the election path read configurations.latest, not the committed configuration: checkLeaderLease counts contacted voters of the latest configuration and demotes the leader when that count is below the latest configuration's quorum size, and quorumSize (used by candidates to decide when they have won) is computed from the same latest configuration. An uncommitted configuration whose quorum requires a server that never answers therefore both blocks commitment and removes the surviving servers' ability to keep or regain leadership.
knowledge.conditions: A node whose configurations.latest includes a voter added by a configuration entry that has not committed, while that voter is unreachable.

knowledge.statement: The timeout accepted by the configuration-change APIs bounds only the attempt to hand the request to the main loop: requestConfigChange returns errorFuture{ErrEnqueueTimeout} if the timer fires before the request is queued, otherwise it returns the future whose Error blocks until the configuration entry commits. A caller cannot use that timeout to learn that the configuration change is stuck.
knowledge.conditions: Any AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer call with a non-zero timeout.

knowledge.statement: On a single-voter cluster, AddVoter for a server that is not running yet commits the configuration change (the leader's own match is recorded against the previous configuration's quorum) and the future completes successfully, after which the only node loses leadership within the lease timeout and remains a Candidate that cannot be re-elected under the configuration it just committed, so client writes are refused with ErrNotLeader until the named server appears; pre-vote keeps its term unchanged throughout, and starting the named server restores leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, a configuration with exactly one voter grown by one voter (so the new configuration's quorum cannot be met by the surviving server), the named server not running, no faults, in-memory transport. Observed with 25 ms sampling for 1500 ms after the call, with the same call on an equivalent cluster whose named server was already running as the control.

knowledge.statement: A wedged replica (conflict-truncation store-error state) does not converge while running, even after the store error is removed, but a restart over the same durable state does converge: after restarting the same stores with a fresh transport at the same address, the certificate, the store's last index and the commit index return to the leader's values and the leader's re-sent entries are stored (certificate (5,3) versus the wedged (4,2), commit 0 to 5).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster, in-memory transport, the store wrapper's error no longer injected; restart modelled as NewRaft over the same log store, stable store and snapshot store with a new transport at the same address and the peers rewired (Shutdown closes the transport it was built with). Observed for four seconds after the restart with 200 ms sampling.

result.summary: Refined the wedge investigation with its margin generalization (a wedged replica costs exactly one unit of commitment quorum margin), adding one behavior on the commitment arithmetic and extending the hypothesis and discriminator to a five-voter escalation measurement for the next execution.

Predicted observations: the certificate stays above the store's real last index indefinitely; the follower's log store never regains the missing indices; the leader's nextIndex for that peer settles at 1 and stays there; and the only in-library repairs (NewRaft re-reading the store at startup, or an InstallSnapshot) are not triggered by this state.
history.discriminator: Stage a legal single-cluster history: 4 voters, the initial leader A is partitioned, A appends entries locally while the majority {B,C,D} elects a new leader at a higher term and commits different entries at the same indices; then arm a legal LogStore wrapper on A (all StoreLogs calls fail with an error, an allowed return from the interface) and heal. Compare, over a bounded window of at least two seconds: A's cached certificate (getLastEntry/LastIndex) against A's store contents (FirstIndex/LastIndex and GetLog of the certificate index); whether A's store ever regains the missing indices or its commit/applied index advances; and the leader's nextIndex for A over time, to show whether the reject/retry cycle restores the same blocking request (nextIndex floored at 1) with no enabled repair. The control is the same conflict and heal with a healthy store: A converges (certificate equals the store's last index and the entries are stored). To distinguish the blocking cause from a mere certificate report, the control must show convergence with the fault absent, and the faulted case must show the store never advancing even though the leader keeps sending.
limitations: The stronger safety consequence remains unclaimed for the reason already recorded: a truncation only happens when the incoming term is not older than the receiver's current term, so the deleted suffix's terms are lower than the truncating leader's, and any voter that accepted that leader's entries has a higher last term and denies the stale claimant.

The wedge claim is a source-derived prediction until executed; the two events it needs (a conflicting suffix truncation and an allowed StoreLogs error in that exact window) must both be staged and stated, and the observation window must be long enough to show the same blocking request being re-entered rather than a one-off rejection.

investigations.question: In the growth sequence the library documents (bootstrap a single voter, then AddVoter the next server), what happens to commitment, leadership and further elections if the newly named server is not running yet, and does the cluster recover once that server appears at the announced address?
investigations.hypothesis: appendConfigurationEntry installs the next configuration as configurations.latest and calls commitment.setConfiguration before the entry is committed, and the new server's match index starts at 0. In the 1-to-2 growth step the new configuration's quorum is 2, so the configuration entry (and any later entry) can never reach a quorum match index while that server is absent. checkLeaderLease counts the voters of the latest configuration, sees one contacted server against a quorum of two, and steps the leader down after the lease expires; elections then need a quorum of the same latest configuration, which the single surviving server cannot supply, so no leader is elected and the cluster stops accepting new entries. The caller's AddVoter timeout does not cover this: requestConfigChange only uses it to bound the enqueue, and the returned future resolves when the configuration commits. Prediction: the cluster stays without a leader and without progress until the announced server appears, at which point the configuration entry commits and the cluster resumes.
investigations.discriminator: Build a real single-voter cluster with MakeCluster(1), obtain the address of a future server from a fresh in-memory transport that is deliberately not wired to the cluster, and call AddVoter on the leader with that address. Record, over a bounded window: the configuration entry index against the leader's commit index, the leader's state and term, whether it ever leaves leadership, whether another node ever becomes leader, whether a later Apply completes, and the future's resolution. Then wire the announced server in (starting a raft on that address with its own empty store) and record whether the configuration commits and progress resumes. The control is the same growth step with the server started and wired before the call, which isolates the absent server as the cause rather than the growth step itself.
limitations: Adding a voter whose process is not running is the caller's input, so the argument rests on the library's own documentation of this sequence and on its stated staging/promotion behaviour, not on an invented caller mistake.

The arithmetic is configuration dependent: growing 2 to 3 or 3 to 4 keeps a quorum among the survivors, so the claim is scoped to configurations whose new quorum cannot be met without the absent server, of which the documented 1-to-2 start is the example.
The transient unavailability window in the observed run will be bounded by the lease and election timeouts; the source-derived part is that no self-repair exists while the server is absent.

knowledge.statement: For an explicit leadership transfer (LeadershipTransferToServer) the leader accepts the caller-supplied target if and only if a followerReplication entry exists for that ServerID in leaderState.replState; the only rejection is a target equal to the local ID ('cannot transfer leadership to itself'). No suffrage test is applied at the API, at initiateLeadershipTransfer, or at the leaderLoop hand-off to leadershipTransfer.
knowledge.conditions: protocolVersion >= 3, node is in Leader state and processing the leadershipTransferCh case on the main thread; the caller supplies an ID present in configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: startStopReplication starts a followerReplication goroutine for every server in configurations.latest whose ID differs from the local ID, with no suffrage filter, so leaderState.replState (the map consulted by the explicit transfer path and by pickServer) also contains Nonvoter members. pickServer, by contrast, skips 'server.Suffrage != Voter', so the targetless transfer path cannot select a non-voter.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state, after appendConfigurationEntry/setLatestConfiguration followed by startStopReplication.

knowledge.statement: On receiving a TimeoutNowRequest a node clears its known leader, sets its state to Candidate and sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer to true, then acknowledges. The handler performs no term comparison (TimeoutNowRequest carries no term), no state check, no suffrage check on the receiver, and no check that the sender is the current leader or a configuration member; runCandidate then skips pre-vote for such a candidate and calls electSelf directly.
knowledge.conditions: The RPC passes checkRPCHeader (protocol version range) and is dispatched from processRPC on the main thread.

knowledge.statement: In requestVote, when a RequestVote arrives with req.Term > currentTerm the receiver first steps down (setState(Follower)) and adopts the higher term, and only afterwards rejects the request because the candidate is not a Voter ('rejecting vote request since node is not a voter'), returning Granted false. Because the step-down precedes the rejection, a term-advancing vote request from an unelectable candidate still removes the receiver from leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a Voter or Leader with a non-empty configurations.latest.Servers, and the candidate passes the inConfiguration check.

knowledge.statement: In appendEntries, when a received entry conflicts with one the node already stores, the node deletes the range [entry.Index, lastLogIdx] via logs.DeleteRange, then stores the replacement entries via logs.StoreLogs. If StoreLogs returns an error the handler logs 'failed to append to logs' and returns before any setLastLog call: the in-memory lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm keep the values they had before the deletion (the code marks this with a TODO), and no other branch in the receive path restores them. The response for that request is left with Success false.
knowledge.conditions: Follower/Candidate state; a.Term not older than the node's current term; at least one received entry whose index is at or below the node's last log index and whose term differs from the stored entry; and an error return from logs.StoreLogs for that call.

knowledge.statement: The in-memory last-log certificate is read through raftState.getLastEntry (and getLastIndex, which takes the maximum of lastLogIndex and lastSnapshotIndex, so a snapshot does not mask a stale log index). Its consumers are: electSelf and preElectSelf, which put it in RequestVoteRequest/RequestPreVoteRequest as LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm; requestVote/requestPreVote, which use it to decide whether to grant a vote; appendEntries, which compares it against PrevLogEntry to validate a leader's previous entry; and Raft.LastIndex, the public accessor. None of these consult the LogStore.
knowledge.conditions: Any node, whenever it campaigns or answers a vote request or validates an AppendEntries previous entry.

knowledge.statement: In the appendEntries entry loop the comparison 'entry.Index > lastLogIdx' uses lastLogIdx read from the in-memory certificate (getLastLog), not from the log store. For an entry at or below that cached index the handler calls logs.GetLog(entry.Index) and returns immediately if it errors, so once the conflicting suffix has been deleted from the store, any re-sent entry covering those indices makes the handler return before StoreLogs is reached. The certificate is never re-derived from the store inside this handler.
knowledge.conditions: Follower or Candidate state with at least one entry in the request whose index is at or below the cached last log index while that index is absent from the store (the state produced by a failed StoreLogs immediately after a conflicting-suffix deletion).

knowledge.statement: On an unsuccessful AppendEntries response the leader sets the peer's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1). When the follower's response carries a LastLog at or above the leader's index, the value settles at 1 (or at the floor) and the leader re-sends the same request, so a follower that rejects for a self-inflicted reason is re-driven with an identical request rather than a snapshot; ErrLogNotFound leading to SEND_SNAP is only produced from the leader's own log store, not from the follower's response.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the follower responds Success=false with a LastLog hint at or above the leader's last index.

knowledge.statement: A single allowed error return from LogStore.StoreLogs in the call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge: its durable log keeps the truncated state (its last index falls to the last surviving index before the conflict), its cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix, its commit and applied indexes stop advancing, and no further StoreLogs call is even attempted, so removing the error afterwards does not restore progress.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, one follower holding an isolated uncommitted tail appended at an earlier term, a higher-term leader with committed replacement entries at the same indices, and exactly one allowed StoreLogs error on the replacement write; the fault may be removed afterwards without changing the outcome. In the observed run the same history with a healthy store converged inside the window (store 1..5, certificate (5,3), commit and applied 5) while the faulted node stayed at store last 2, certificate (4,2) and commit and applied 2 for 2.7 s.

knowledge.statement: When the wedged replica from the conflict-truncation store-error state is one of three voters, the cluster cannot commit any new entry after a single further voter loss: the leader accepts the entry into its own log (store and certificate advance to the new index) but its commit index stays at the value it had before and the client's apply future never completes, whereas the control run of the identical history without the store error commits the same entry as soon as the peer-loss phase begins. The wedged replica's store last index and StoreLogs attempt counter are unchanged across the phase, so its match index cannot advance and the quorum of match indexes can no longer include the new entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport; one voter left in the conflict-truncation store-error state (store truncated, cached certificate stale, no further store writes); one further voter removed; one client entry applied on the remaining leader. Observed for 1500 ms with 25 ms sampling, with the matching control run in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, without waiting for it to commit, sets configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration, which rebuilds the match-index map so that every voter of the new configuration is counted, with servers that have never answered starting at 0. The quorum decisions for commitment therefore use the new configuration from that moment, while configurations.committed still describes the old one.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; any successful configuration change request (AddVoter, AddNonvoter, DemoteVoter, RemoveServer) whose entry has been appended but not yet committed.

knowledge.statement: Both the leader lease check and the election path read configurations.latest, not the committed configuration: checkLeaderLease counts contacted voters of the latest configuration and demotes the leader when that count is below the latest configuration's quorum size, and quorumSize (used by candidates to decide when they have won) is computed from the same latest configuration. An uncommitted configuration whose quorum requires a server that never answers therefore both blocks commitment and removes the surviving servers' ability to keep or regain leadership.
knowledge.conditions: A node whose configurations.latest includes a voter added by a configuration entry that has not committed, while that voter is unreachable.

knowledge.statement: The timeout accepted by the configuration-change APIs bounds only the attempt to hand the request to the main loop: requestConfigChange returns errorFuture{ErrEnqueueTimeout} if the timer fires before the request is queued, otherwise it returns the future whose Error blocks until the configuration entry commits. A caller cannot use that timeout to learn that the configuration change is stuck.
knowledge.conditions: Any AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer call with a non-zero timeout.

knowledge.statement: On a single-voter cluster, AddVoter for a server that is not running yet commits the configuration change (the leader's own match is recorded against the previous configuration's quorum) and the future completes successfully, after which the only node loses leadership within the lease timeout and remains a Candidate that cannot be re-elected under the configuration it just committed, so client writes are refused with ErrNotLeader until the named server appears; pre-vote keeps its term unchanged throughout, and starting the named server restores leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, a configuration with exactly one voter grown by one voter (so the new configuration's quorum cannot be met by the surviving server), the named server not running, no faults, in-memory transport. Observed with 25 ms sampling for 1500 ms after the call, with the same call on an equivalent cluster whose named server was already running as the control.

knowledge.statement: A wedged replica (conflict-truncation store-error state) does not converge while running, even after the store error is removed, but a restart over the same durable state does converge: after restarting the same stores with a fresh transport at the same address, the certificate, the store's last index and the commit index return to the leader's values and the leader's re-sent entries are stored (certificate (5,3) versus the wedged (4,2), commit 0 to 5).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster, in-memory transport, the store wrapper's error no longer injected; restart modelled as NewRaft over the same log store, stable store and snapshot store with a new transport at the same address and the peers rewired (Shutdown closes the transport it was built with). Observed for four seconds after the restart with 200 ms sampling.

knowledge.statement: commitment keeps one match index per voter of the current configuration and takes the quorum match index as the middle of the sorted values, so a voter whose stored log can never advance holds its slot at the stuck index for as long as the configuration stands. The wedged replica therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin: the remaining voters must be able to form a quorum on their own, which in a three-voter configuration is impossible once one other voter is gone and in a five-voter configuration only becomes impossible when two other voters are gone.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; a voter whose durable log is stuck below the leader's committed prefix while it remains a member of configurations.latest; commitment.setConfiguration has been applied for that configuration.
